+  // Refuse-closed: pre-F-127 archives that lack the later capture fields,
~
+  // receipt/proposal/binding digest mismatches, archived-seal
~
+  // schemaVersion/runId/bindingDigest mismatches, and active/corrupt/one-shot
~
+  // runs (those are never GC'd).
~
+  const runDirectoryReclaimed = !existsSync(join(runDirectory, 'spec.json'))
~
+    && !existsSync(join(runDirectory, 'terminal.json'));
~
+  if (runDirectoryReclaimed) {
~
+    observedTerminalDigest = args.binding.terminalDigest;
~
+    observedProposalDigest = receipt.evidenceProposalDigest;
~
+    proposalArtifacts = receipt.evidenceProposalDigest ? ['evidence-proposal.json'] : [];
~
+    observedSpecDigest = receipt.specDigest;
~
+    observedEventJournalDigest = receipt.eventJournalDigest;
~
+    observedResultDigest = receipt.resultDigest;
~
+  } else try {
~
+    observedTerminalDigest = sha256(readFileSync(terminalPath, 'utf8'));
~
+    observedProposalDigest = proposal
~
+      ? sha256(readFileSync(join(runDirectory, 'evidence-proposal.json'), 'utf8'))
~
+      : null;
~
+    proposalArtifacts = readdirSync(runDirectory)
~
+      .filter(name => /^evidence-proposal(?:[.-].*)?\.json$/.test(name));
~
+    observedSpecDigest = sha256(readFileSync(join(runDirectory, 'spec.json'), 'utf8'));
~
+    observedEventJournalDigest = existsSync(join(runDirectory, 'events.jsonl'))
~
+      ? sha256(readFileSync(join(runDirectory, 'events.jsonl'), 'utf8'))
~
+      : sha256('');
~
+    observedResultDigest = existsSync(join(runDirectory, 'result.json'))
~
+      ? sha256(readFileSync(join(runDirectory, 'result.json'), 'utf8'))
~
+      : null;
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    const diagnostic = failedDiagnostic();
~
+    const cause = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
~
+    return {
~
+      valid: false,
~
+      reason: `${diagnostic.reasons.join(',')} (runtime artifact read failed: ${cause})`,
~
+      diagnostic,
~
+      receipt: null,
~
+      proposal: null,
~
+    };
~
+  }
~
+  const shapeValid = args.binding.schemaVersion === 'lattice.managed_review_evidence_binding.v1'
~
+    && proposal?.schemaVersion === 'lattice.managed_review_evidence_proposal.v1'
~
+    && (proposal?.conclusion !== 'findings'
~
+      || (Array.isArray(proposal.findings)
~
+        && proposal.findings.length > 0
~
+        && proposal.findings.every(isStrictManagedReviewFindingProposal)))
~
+    && Number.isFinite(Date.parse(args.binding.importedAt))
~
+    && args.binding.providerHost === args.expected.providerHost;
~
+  const exactEvidenceMatches = (() => {
~
+    if (!args.evidence) return true;
~
+    if (!proposal) return false;
~
+    if (args.evidence.kind === 'pass') {
~
+      if (proposal.conclusion !== 'pass' || args.binding.proposalFindingIndex !== undefined) return false;
~
+      return digestCanonicalJson({
~
+        note: args.evidence.pass.note,
~
+        readManifest: args.evidence.pass.readManifest,
~
+        readLog: args.evidence.pass.readLog,
~
+        readDiagnostics: args.evidence.pass.readDiagnostics,
~
+      }) === digestCanonicalJson({
~
+        note: proposal.note,
~
+        readManifest: proposal.readManifest,
~
+        readLog: proposal.readLog,
~
+        readDiagnostics: proposal.readDiagnostics,
~
+      });
~
+    }
~
+    if (proposal.conclusion !== 'findings') return false;
~
+    const index = args.binding.proposalFindingIndex;
~
+    if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index! < 0) return false;
~
+    const candidate = proposal.findings?.[index!];
~
+    if (!candidate) return false;
~
+    // B-137a:F-100 — `status` is LIFECYCLE state, not provider-authored content.
~
+    // A provider always authors a finding as 'open'; the host later moves it to
~
+    // 'resolved'/'dismissed' via finding_resolve, which mutates the stored record
~
+    // in place. Comparing the live status against a hardcoded 'open' therefore
~
+    // made every managed finding's receipt invalid the moment it was resolved,
~
+    // and `managed_receipt_invalid` is absent from SUPERSEDED_PASS_ISSUE_CODES,
~
+    // so it reached evidenceState.invalid and hard-blocked REVIEW→TEST at
~
+    // machine.ts BEFORE the blocking-severity filter — i.e. resolving a managed
~
+    // finding permanently blocked the gate regardless of its severity.
~
+    //
~
+    // Fix: exclude the mutable lifecycle status from the authorship digest on
~
+    // BOTH sides. Every provider-authored field (desc/severity/category/
~
+    // evidenceState/uncertaintyReason/files/read provenance) stays byte-bound,
~
+    // so tampering with real authored content is still rejected; only the
~
+    // host-owned lifecycle transition is permitted to move.
~
+    //
~
+    // No separate "authored status must be open" guard is needed: the provider
~
+    // proposal type (ManagedReviewEvidenceFindingProposal in managed-host-run.ts)
~
+    // has NO status field, so a provider structurally cannot author one and the
~
+    // old literal 'open' was describing the type, not validating input.
~
+    return digestCanonicalJson({
~
+      desc: args.evidence.finding.desc,
~
+      severity: args.evidence.finding.severity,
~
+      category: args.evidence.finding.category,
~
+      evidenceState: args.evidence.finding.evidenceState ?? 'verified',
~
+      uncertaintyReason: args.evidence.finding.uncertaintyReason,
~
+      files: args.evidence.finding.files ?? [],
~
+      readManifest: args.evidence.finding.readManifest,
~
+      readLog: args.evidence.finding.readLog,
~
+      readDiagnostics: args.evidence.finding.readDiagnostics,
~
+    }) === digestCanonicalJson({
~
+      desc: candidate.desc,
~
+      severity: candidate.severity,
~
+      category: candidate.category,
~
+      evidenceState: candidate.evidenceState ?? 'verified',
~
+      uncertaintyReason: candidate.uncertaintyReason,
~
+      files: candidate.files ?? [],
~
+      readManifest: proposal.readManifest,
~
+      readLog: proposal.readLog,
~
+      readDiagnostics: proposal.readDiagnostics,
~
+    });
~
+  })();
~
+  const externalImportSealMatches = (() => {
~
+    if (!args.evidence) return true;
~
+    // B-137a:F-127 / F-132 — archive-backed so a reclaimed run's imported
~
+    // evidence stays verifiable. readManagedReviewImportSeal returns the live
~
+    // files when present and otherwise the archived texts, but only after
~
+    // re-digesting the binding against the archive's recorded
~
+    // evidenceBindingDigest and checking the archived seal's schemaVersion,
~
+    // runId, and bindingDigest. This function also parses sealText and repeats
~
+    // those live-path seal checks so a malformed or altered seal cannot admit
~
+    // gate-consumed evidence.
~
+    const seal = (() => {
~
+      try { return readManagedReviewImportSeal(args.root, args.binding.runId); } catch { return null; }
~
+    })();
~
+    if (!seal) return false;
~
+    try {
~
+      const external = JSON.parse(seal.bindingText) as Record<string, unknown>;
~
+      const sealRecord = JSON.parse(seal.sealText) as Record<string, unknown>;
~
+      const evidenceId = args.evidence.kind === 'pass' ? args.evidence.pass.id : args.evidence.finding.id;
~
+      return external.schemaVersion === 'lattice.managed_review_evidence_import.v1'
~
+        && external.runId === args.binding.runId
~
+        && external.receiptId === args.binding.receiptId
~
+        && external.storyId === args.storyId
~
+        && external.reviewRunId === args.reviewRunId
~
+        && external.lane === args.lane
~
+        && external.importedAt === args.binding.importedAt
~
+        && Array.isArray(external.importedIds)
~
+        && external.importedIds.includes(evidenceId)
~
+        && sealRecord.schemaVersion === 'lattice.managed_review_evidence_binding_seal.v1'
~
+        && sealRecord.runId === args.binding.runId
~
+        && sealRecord.bindingDigest === sha256(seal.bindingText);
~
+    } catch {
~
+      return false;
~
+    }
~
+  })();
~
+  const semanticDigestValid = proposal !== null
~
+    && proposalArtifacts.length === 1
~
+    && proposalArtifacts[0] === 'evidence-proposal.json'
~
+    && receipt.evidenceProposalDigest !== null
~
+    && receipt.evidenceProposalDigest === args.binding.proposalDigest
~
+    && observedProposalDigest === receipt.evidenceProposalDigest
~
+    && observedSpecDigest === receipt.specDigest
~
+    && observedEventJournalDigest === receipt.eventJournalDigest
~
+    && observedResultDigest === receipt.resultDigest
~
+    && externalImportSealMatches
~
+    && exactEvidenceMatches;
~
+  const receiptValid = receipt.receiptId === args.binding.receiptId
~
+    && receipt.terminalDigest === args.binding.terminalDigest
~
+    && observedTerminalDigest === args.binding.terminalDigest
~
+    && receipt.state === 'completed'
~
+    && receipt.replacementSafe === true
~
+    && receipt.processCleanup?.reaped === true
~
+    && receipt.processCleanup.residualProcessGroup === false;
~
+  const subjectMatches = proposal !== null
~
+    && proposal.providerAgent === args.binding.providerAgent
~
+    && args.binding.providerAgent === args.agent
~
+    && args.agent === args.lane
~
+    && proposal.lane === args.lane
~
+    && args.binding.lane === args.lane
~
+    && args.binding.reviewRunId === args.reviewRunId
~
+    && proposal.reviewRunId === args.reviewRunId
~
+    && runBinding.profile === 'managed_reviewer'
~
+    && runBinding.host === args.binding.providerHost
~
+    && runBinding.agentType === args.agent
~
+    && runBinding.lane === args.lane
~
+    && runBinding.reviewRunId === args.reviewRunId;
~
+  const sealedManagedPromptDigest = runBinding.reviewBinding?.managedPromptDigest;
~
+  const expectedManagedPromptDigest = sealedManagedPromptDigest ?? args.expected.managedPromptDigest;
~
+  const sealedManagedPromptDigestValid = sealedManagedPromptDigest === undefined
~
+    || /^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(sealedManagedPromptDigest);
~
+  const reviewTupleMatches = runBinding.reviewBinding !== null
~
+    && runBinding.reviewBinding.headHash === args.expected.headHash
~
+    && runBinding.reviewBinding.materialHash === args.expected.materialHash
~
+    && runBinding.reviewBinding.storyFilesHash === args.expected.storyFilesHash
~
+    && runBinding.reviewBinding.promptHash === args.expected.promptHash
~
+    && runBinding.reviewBinding.envelopeId === args.expected.envelopeId
~
+    && args.binding.headHash === args.expected.headHash
~
+    && args.binding.materialHash === args.expected.materialHash
~
+    && args.binding.storyFilesHash === args.expected.storyFilesHash
~
+    && args.binding.promptHash === args.expected.promptHash
~
+    && args.binding.envelopeId === args.expected.envelopeId
~
+    && sealedManagedPromptDigestValid
~
+    && args.binding.managedPromptDigest === expectedManagedPromptDigest
~
+    && runBinding.promptDigest === expectedManagedPromptDigest;
~
+  const storyMatches = proposal?.storyId === args.storyId
~
+    && runBinding.storyId === args.storyId;
~
+  const diagnostic = buildProofAdmissibilityDiagnostic({
~
+    artifactKind: 'managed-review-evidence',
~
+    artifactId: args.binding.receiptId,
~
+    consumer: 'REVIEW',
~
+    claim: 'review-pass',
~
+    mode: 'enforce',
~
+    enforcedConsumers: ['REVIEW'],
~
+    checks: {
~
+      schemaVersion: args.binding.schemaVersion,
~
+      strictShapeValid: shapeValid,
~
+      semanticDigestValid,
~
+      signatureOrReceiptBindingValid: receiptValid,
~
+      temporalAndMaterialBindingValid: subjectMatches && storyMatches && reviewTupleMatches,
~
+      subjectMatches,
~
+      storyMatches,
~
+      gatePhaseMatches: true,
~
+      producerBoundaryTrusted: receiptValid && subjectMatches && reviewTupleMatches,
~
+    },
~
+  });
~
+  const valid = diagnostic.allowed && !diagnostic.blocking;
~
+  return {
~
+    valid,
~
+    reason: valid ? 'managed_review_evidence_admissible' : diagnostic.reasons.join(','),
~
+    diagnostic,
~
+    receipt,
~
+    proposal,
~
+  };
~
+}
~
~
+export function createManagedReviewEvidenceBinding(args: {
~
+  root: string;
~
+  storyId: string;
~
+  providerAgent: string;
~
+  lane: string;
~
+  reviewRunId: string;
~
+  runId: string;
~
+  receiptId: string;
~
+  expected: ManagedReviewExpectedBinding;
~
+  importedAt?: string;
~
+}): { binding: ManagedReviewEvidenceBinding; verification: ManagedReviewEvidenceVerification } {
~
+  let receipt: ManagedHostRunReceipt | null = null;
~
+  try {
~
+    receipt = managedHostRunReceipt(args.root, args.runId);
~
+  } catch {
~
+    // The shared evaluator below classifies missing/non-terminal receipt input;
~
+    // the importer does not maintain a parallel allow/deny vocabulary.
~
+  }
~
+  const binding: ManagedReviewEvidenceBinding = {
~
+    schemaVersion: 'lattice.managed_review_evidence_binding.v1',
~
+    runId: args.runId,
~
+    receiptId: args.receiptId,
~
+    proposalDigest: receipt?.evidenceProposalDigest ?? '',
~
+    terminalDigest: receipt?.terminalDigest ?? '',
~
+    importedAt: args.importedAt ?? new Date().toISOString(),
~
+    providerAgent: args.providerAgent,
~
+    providerHost: args.expected.providerHost,
~
+    lane: args.lane,
~
+    reviewRunId: args.reviewRunId,
~
+    headHash: args.expected.headHash,
~
+    materialHash: args.expected.materialHash,
~
+    storyFilesHash: args.expected.storyFilesHash,
~
+    promptHash: args.expected.promptHash,
~
+    envelopeId: args.expected.envelopeId,
~
+    managedPromptDigest: args.expected.managedPromptDigest,
~
+  };
~
+  const verification = verifyManagedReviewEvidence({
~
+    root: args.root,
~
+    storyId: args.storyId,
~
+    agent: args.providerAgent,
~
+    lane: args.lane,
~
+    reviewRunId: args.reviewRunId,
~
+    binding,
~
+    expected: args.expected,
~
+  });
~
+  if (!verification.valid) {
~
+    throw new Error(`managed_review_evidence_import: ${verification.reason}`);
~
+  }
~
+  return { binding, verification };
~
+}
~

+/**
~
+ * Ledger-independent provider-process admission.
~
+ *
~
+ * Usage accounting may be disabled, but every Lattice-owned provider spawn
~
+ * still competes for the same atomic slot registry. This module is the small
~
+ * adapter used by all Lattice-owned provider launch sites.
~
+ */
~
~
+import {
~
+  acquireProviderProcessSlot,
~
+  providerProcessSlotsDir,
~
+  releaseProviderProcessSlotBestEffort,
~
+  resolveProviderProcessMaxConcurrent,
~
+  resolveProviderProcessSlotStaleMs,
~
+  scanLiveProviderProcessSlots,
~
+  transferProviderProcessSlotToProvider,
~
+  type AcquiredProviderProcessSlot,
~
+  type ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor,
~
+  type ProviderRegistryLockTiming,
~
+  type ProviderRegistryMutationOps,
~
+} from './provider-process-registry.js';
~
~
+export interface ProviderProcessAdmissionRequest {
~
+  root: string;
~
+  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
~
+  host: string;
~
+  storyId: string | null;
~
+  agentType: string;
~
+  startedAt?: string;
~
+  pid?: number;
~
+}
~
~
+export interface ProviderProcessAdmission {
~
+  admitted: boolean;
~
+  slot: AcquiredProviderProcessSlot | null;
~
+  cap: number;
~
+  liveRuns: ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor[];
~
+}
~
~
+/** Internal release seam; production callers use the fail-safe defaults. */
~
+export interface ProviderProcessAdmissionReleaseOptions {
~
+  onFailure?: (error: unknown) => void;
~
+  lockTiming?: ProviderRegistryLockTiming;
~
+  mutationOps?: ProviderRegistryMutationOps;
~
+}
~
~
+export function acquireProviderProcessAdmission(
~
+  request: ProviderProcessAdmissionRequest,
~
+): ProviderProcessAdmission {
~
+  const dir = providerProcessSlotsDir(request.root);
~
+  const cap = resolveProviderProcessMaxConcurrent(request.env);
~
+  const staleMs = resolveProviderProcessSlotStaleMs(request.env);
~
+  const slot = acquireProviderProcessSlot(dir, cap, staleMs, Date.now(), {
~
+    pid: request.pid ?? process.pid,
~
+    startedAt: request.startedAt ?? new Date().toISOString(),
~
+    host: request.host,
~
+    storyId: request.storyId,
~
+    agentType: request.agentType,
~
+  });
~
+  return {
~
+    admitted: slot !== null,
~
+    slot,
~
+    cap,
~
+    // B-137a:F-126 — DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY, and deliberately a post-refusal snapshot.
~
+    //
~
+    // The admission DECISION is already made above, atomically under the
~
+    // registry lock. This scan runs after that lock is released, with a fresh
~
+    // Date.now(), so it can legitimately disagree with the decision: a slot
~
+    // freed in between makes the list shorter than `cap` even though the
~
+    // refusal was correct at decision time. That is why it never feeds a gate.
~
+    //
~
+    // Holding the lock across the scan would make the two agree but would
~
+    // serialize every refusal behind a directory walk, adding contention to the
~
+    // exact path that is already saturated. The snapshot is described as
~
+    // approximate at its user-facing consumer (host-run.ts refusalDetail)
~
+    // instead of being presented as an authoritative count.
~
+    liveRuns: slot ? [] : scanLiveProviderProcessSlots(dir, Date.now(), staleMs),
~
+  };
~
+}
~
~
+export function releaseProviderProcessAdmission(
~
+  admission: ProviderProcessAdmission | null,
~
+  options: ProviderProcessAdmissionReleaseOptions = {},
~
+): void {
~
+  if (!admission?.slot) return;
~
+  releaseProviderProcessSlotBestEffort(
~
+    admission.slot.file,
~
+    admission.slot.token,
~
+    options.onFailure,
~
+    options.lockTiming,
~
+    options.mutationOps,
~
+  );
~
+}
~
~
+export function transferProviderProcessAdmissionToProvider(
~
+  admission: ProviderProcessAdmission | null,
~
+  identity: {
~
+    pid: number;
~
+    pgid: number | null;
~
+    spawnedAt: string;
~
+    startFingerprint: string | null;
~
+    processGroupIsolated: boolean;
~
+  },
~
+): boolean {
~
+  if (!admission?.slot) return false;
~
+  return transferProviderProcessSlotToProvider(admission.slot.file, admission.slot.token, identity);
~
+}
~

+/**
~
+ * Canonical, ledger-independent provider-process capacity registry.
~
+ *
~
+ * Admission is an atomic exclusive create of one of a fixed set of numbered
~
+ * slots. Usage accounting may be disabled; this registry never is. A recorded
~
+ * live pid is never reclaimed because of age alone, and release is guarded by
~
+ * the acquire-minted ownership token.
~
+ */
~
~
+import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
~
+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
~
+import {
~
+  mkdirSync,
~
+  readdirSync,
~
+  readFileSync,
~
+  statSync,
~
+  unlinkSync,
~
+  renameSync,
~
+  writeFileSync,
~
+} from 'node:fs';
~
+import { hostname } from 'node:os';
~
+import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
~
+import {
~
+  acquireMkdirLock,
~
+  type ExistingMkdirLockSnapshot,
~
+  type ExistingMkdirLockState,
~
+} from './mkdir-lock.js';
~
+import { resolveCanonicalRuntimeProjectRoot } from './runtime-artifact-registry.js';
~
~
+const PROVIDER_PROCESS_SLOTS_RELATIVE = join('.lattice', 'runtime', 'provider-process-slots');
~
+export const PROVIDER_PROCESS_MAX_CONCURRENT_DEFAULT = 4;
~
+export const PROVIDER_PROCESS_SLOT_STALE_MS_DEFAULT = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
~
~
+export interface ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor {
~
+  pid: number;
~
+  startedAt: string;
~
+  host: string;
~
+  storyId: string | null;
~
+  agentType: string;
~
+}
~
~
+export interface ProviderProcessSlotMeta extends ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor {}
~
~
+export interface ProviderProcessSlotFileMeta extends ProviderProcessSlotMeta {
~
+  token: string;
~
+  providerPid?: number;
~
+  providerPgid?: number;
~
+  providerSpawnedAt?: string;
~
+  providerStartFingerprint?: string;
~
+  providerProcessGroupIsolated?: boolean;
~
+}
~
~
+export interface AcquiredProviderProcessSlot {
~
+  file: string;
~
+  token: string;
~
+}
~
~
+export interface ProviderRegistryLockTiming {
~
+  deadlineMs?: number;
~
+  staleMs?: number;
~
+  pollMs?: number;
~
+}
~
~
+export interface ProviderRegistryMutationOps {
~
+  unlink(file: string): void;
~
+}
~
~
+/** Test-only observation/mutation seams for a replacement between stale-read and reclaim. */
~
+export interface ProviderRegistryScanHooks {
~
+  beforeReclaimRecheck?(file: string): void;
~
+  unlinkForReclaim?(file: string): void;
~
+}
~
~
+const DEFAULT_PROVIDER_REGISTRY_MUTATION_OPS: ProviderRegistryMutationOps = {
~
+  unlink: unlinkSync,
~
+};
~
~
+type SlotOccupant =
~
+  | { state: 'valid'; pid: number; token: string | null; meta: Record<string, unknown> }
~
+  | { state: 'corrupt'; identity: string }
~
+  | { state: 'missing' };
~
~
+function corruptSlotIdentity(file: string, raw: string): string {
~
+  try {
~
+    const stat = statSync(file);
~
+    return `${stat.dev}:${stat.ino}:${stat.size}:${stat.mtimeMs}:${raw}`;
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    return `unstatable:${(error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? 'unknown'}:${raw}`;
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+function ownString(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string | null {
~
+  if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, key)) return null;
~
+  return typeof value[key] === 'string' ? value[key] as string : null;
~
+}
~
~
+function ownNumber(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): number | null {
~
+  if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, key)) return null;
~
+  return typeof value[key] === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value[key]) ? value[key] as number : null;
~
+}
~
~
+function readSlotOccupant(file: string): SlotOccupant {
~
+  let raw: string;
~
+  try {
~
+    raw = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    return (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT'
~
+      ? { state: 'missing' }
~
+      : { state: 'corrupt', identity: corruptSlotIdentity(file, '') };
~
+  }
~
+  try {
~
+    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as unknown;
~
+    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) {
~
+      return { state: 'corrupt', identity: corruptSlotIdentity(file, raw) };
~
+    }
~
+    const meta = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
~
+    const pid = ownNumber(meta, 'pid');
~
+    if (pid === null) return { state: 'corrupt', identity: corruptSlotIdentity(file, raw) };
~
+    return { state: 'valid', pid, token: ownString(meta, 'token'), meta };
~
+  } catch {
~
+    return { state: 'corrupt', identity: corruptSlotIdentity(file, raw) };
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+function sameSlotOccupant(left: SlotOccupant, right: SlotOccupant): boolean {
~
+  if (left.state !== right.state) return false;
~
+  if (left.state === 'valid' && right.state === 'valid') {
~
+    return left.pid === right.pid && left.token === right.token;
~
+  }
~
+  if (left.state === 'corrupt' && right.state === 'corrupt') {
~
+    return left.identity === right.identity;
~
+  }
~
+  return true;
~
+}
~
~
+function pidAlive(pid: number): boolean {
~
+  if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return false;
~
+  try {
~
+    process.kill(pid, 0);
~
+    return true;
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    return (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EPERM';
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+function processGroupAlive(pgid: number): boolean {
~
+  if (!Number.isInteger(pgid) || pgid <= 1 || process.platform === 'win32') return false;
~
+  try {
~
+    process.kill(-pgid, 0);
~
+    return true;
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    return (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EPERM';
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+function slotReclaimable(occupant: SlotOccupant, file: string, now: number, staleMs: number): boolean {
~
+  if (occupant.state === 'missing') return true;
~
+  if (occupant.state === 'valid') {
~
+    const isolated = occupant.meta.providerProcessGroupIsolated === true;
~
+    const providerPgid = ownNumber(occupant.meta, 'providerPgid');
~
+    // Once the admission has transferred to an isolated provider group, the
~
+    // group—not the supervising worker—is the capacity owner. A crashed worker
~
+    // may leave children alive, so reclaim only after the exact PGID disappears.
~
+    if (isolated && providerPgid !== null && processGroupAlive(providerPgid)) return false;
~
+    return !pidAlive(occupant.pid);
~
+  }
~
+  try {
~
+    const ageMs = now - statSync(file).mtimeMs;
~
+    return !Number.isFinite(ageMs) || ageMs > staleMs;
~
+  } catch {
~
+    // Fail closed: an existing slot we cannot stat still occupies capacity.
~
+    return false;
~
+  }
~
+}

~

~
+export function writeProviderProcessSlotExclusive(
~
+  file: string,
~
+  meta: ProviderProcessSlotFileMeta,
~
+): boolean {
~
+  try {
~
+    writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(meta), { encoding: 'utf8', flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 });
~
+    return true;
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EEXIST') return false;
~
+    throw error;
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+interface ProviderProcessSlotScan {
~
+  live: ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor[];
~
+  occupiedCount: number;
~
+}
~
~
+function scanProviderProcessSlotsUnlocked(
~
+  dir: string,
~
+  now: number,
~
+  staleMs: number,
~
+  hooks: ProviderRegistryScanHooks = {},
~
+): ProviderProcessSlotScan {
~
+  let entries: string[];
~
+  try {
~
+    entries = readdirSync(dir);
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return { live: [], occupiedCount: 0 };
~
+    const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? 'unknown';
~
+    const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
~
+    throw new Error(`provider-process-registry slots directory unreadable (${code}): ${detail}`);
~
+  }
~
+  const live: ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor[] = [];
~
+  let occupiedCount = 0;
~
+  for (const name of entries) {
~
+    if (!name.endsWith('.json')) continue;
~
+    const file = join(dir, name);
~
+    const occupant = readSlotOccupant(file);
~
+    if (slotReclaimable(occupant, file, now, staleMs)) {
~
+      hooks.beforeReclaimRecheck?.(file);
~
+      const rechecked = readSlotOccupant(file);
~
+      if (occupant.state !== 'missing' && sameSlotOccupant(rechecked, occupant)) {
~
+        try { (hooks.unlinkForReclaim ?? unlinkSync)(file); } catch { /* re-read below decides occupancy */ }
~
+        // A failed unlink is not a benign reclaim. Re-read its exact path: it
~
+        // only stops consuming capacity once absence is proven. This covers an
~
+        // EACCES/unlink failure as well as a concurrent replacement.
~
+        const afterUnlink = readSlotOccupant(file);
~
+        if (afterUnlink.state === 'missing') continue;
~
+        occupiedCount += 1;
~
+        if (afterUnlink.state === 'valid') {
~
+          live.push({
~
+            pid: afterUnlink.pid,
~
+            startedAt: ownString(afterUnlink.meta, 'startedAt') ?? '',
~
+            host: ownString(afterUnlink.meta, 'host') ?? '',
~
+            storyId: ownString(afterUnlink.meta, 'storyId'),
~
+            agentType: ownString(afterUnlink.meta, 'agentType') ?? '',
~
+          });
~
+        }
~
+        continue;
~
+      }
~
+      // A changed occupant is never ours to reclaim. It consumes capacity even
~
+      // if a second observation looks reclaimable: retrying here could admit a
~
+      // slot-0 holder beside a replacement in a high-index slot.
~
+      if (rechecked.state === 'missing') continue;
~
+      occupiedCount += 1;
~
+      if (rechecked.state === 'valid') {
~
+        live.push({
~
+          pid: rechecked.pid,
~
+          startedAt: ownString(rechecked.meta, 'startedAt') ?? '',
~
+          host: ownString(rechecked.meta, 'host') ?? '',
~
+          storyId: ownString(rechecked.meta, 'storyId'),
~
+          agentType: ownString(rechecked.meta, 'agentType') ?? '',
~
+        });
~
+      }
~
+      continue;
~
+    }
~
+    // A fresh malformed slot has no safe descriptor to show to callers, but
~
+    // cannot be reclaimed either. It must still consume capacity: otherwise a
~
+    // cap lowered below a non-reclaimable high index can admit past its limit.
~
+    occupiedCount += 1;
~
+    if (occupant.state !== 'valid') continue;
~
+    live.push({
~
+      pid: occupant.pid,
~
+      startedAt: ownString(occupant.meta, 'startedAt') ?? '',
~
+      host: ownString(occupant.meta, 'host') ?? '',
~
+      storyId: ownString(occupant.meta, 'storyId'),
~
+      agentType: ownString(occupant.meta, 'agentType') ?? '',
~
+    });
~
+  }
~
+  return { live, occupiedCount };
~
+}
~
~
+function currentProcessStartTimeMs(): number {
~
+  return Math.floor(Date.now() - process.uptime() * 1_000);
~
+}
~
~
+function sameProcessStart(left: number | undefined, right: number | undefined): boolean {
~
+  if (left === undefined || right === undefined) return true;
~
+  return Math.abs(left - right) <= 2_000;
~
+}
~
~
+type ProviderRegistryLockPidState = 'active' | 'stale' | 'unknown';
~
~
+export interface ProviderRegistryLockObservationOps {
~
+  inspectPid?: (pid: number) => ProviderRegistryLockPidState;
~
+  observeProcessStartTimeMs?: (pid: number) => number | undefined;
~
+}
~
~
+function inspectProviderRegistryLockPid(pid: number): ProviderRegistryLockPidState {
~
+  try {
~
+    process.kill(pid, 0);
~
+    return 'active';
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
~
+    if (code === 'ESRCH') return 'stale';
~
+    if (code === 'EPERM') return 'active';
~
+    return 'unknown';
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+/**
~
+ * Best-effort foreign-PID start identity, using ps elapsed time rather than a
~
+ * signal or a provider launch. An unavailable platform/process observation is
~
+ * deliberately not treated as proof of staleness.
~
+ */
~
+function observeProviderRegistryProcessStartTimeMs(pid: number): number | undefined {
~
+  if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0 || process.platform === 'win32') return undefined;
~
+  try {
~
+    const raw = execFileSync('ps', ['-o', 'etimes=', '-p', String(pid)], {
~
+      encoding: 'utf8',
~
+      timeout: 1_000,
~
+      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],
~
+    }).trim();
~
+    const elapsedSeconds = Number(raw);
~
+    return Number.isFinite(elapsedSeconds) && elapsedSeconds >= 0
~
+      ? Math.floor(Date.now() - elapsedSeconds * 1_000)
~
+      : undefined;
~
+  } catch {
~
+    return undefined;
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+/**
~
+ * Classify an existing registry lock with PID-reuse protection for every local
~
+ * holder, not only this process. If a persisted start identity cannot be read
~
+ * back safely after the PID was observed live, retain it as active rather than
~
+ * falling through to mkdir-lock's age-based unknown-lock reclamation.
~
+ */
~
+export function classifyProviderRegistryLock(
~
+  snapshot: ExistingMkdirLockSnapshot,
~
+  ops: ProviderRegistryLockObservationOps = {},
~
+): ExistingMkdirLockState {
~
+  const holder = snapshot.holder;
~
+  if (!holder || holder.hostname !== hostname()) return 'unknown';
~
+  if (!Number.isInteger(holder.pid) || holder.pid <= 0) return 'unknown';
~
+  const pidState = (ops.inspectPid ?? inspectProviderRegistryLockPid)(holder.pid);
~
+  if (pidState !== 'active') return pidState;
~
+  if (holder.processStartTimeMs !== undefined) {
~
+    const observedStart = (ops.observeProcessStartTimeMs ?? observeProviderRegistryProcessStartTimeMs)(holder.pid);
~
+    // The PID liveness probe succeeded. A missing start-time observation does
~
+    // not demonstrate reuse, so fail closed: generic unknown-lock aging must
~
+    // not reclaim a potentially live provider-registry lock.
~
+    if (observedStart === undefined) return 'active';
~
+    if (!sameProcessStart(holder.processStartTimeMs, observedStart)) return 'stale';
~
+  }
~
+  return 'active';
~
+}
~
~
+function withProviderRegistryLock<T>(
~
+  dir: string,
~
+  fn: () => T,
~
+  timing: ProviderRegistryLockTiming = {},
~
+): T {
~
+  const lock = acquireMkdirLock(`${dir}.lock`, {
~
+    label: 'provider-process-registry',
~
+    deadlineMs: timing.deadlineMs ?? 30_000,
~
+    staleMs: timing.staleMs ?? 10_000,
~
+    pollMs: timing.pollMs ?? 10,
~
+    requireHolderToken: true,
~
+    classifyExistingLock: classifyProviderRegistryLock,
~
+    holderInfo: {
~
+      pid: process.pid,
~
+      hostname: hostname(),
~
+      command: 'provider-process-registry mutation',
~
+      acquiredAt: new Date().toISOString(),
~
+      lockId: randomUUID(),
~
+      processStartTimeMs: currentProcessStartTimeMs(),
~
+    },
~
+  });
~
+  try {
~
+    return fn();
~
+  } finally {
~
+    lock.release();
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+export function scanLiveProviderProcessSlots(
~
+  dir: string,
~
+  now: number,
~
+  staleMs: number,
~
+  lockTiming: ProviderRegistryLockTiming = {},
~
+): ProviderProcessLiveDescriptor[] {
~
+  return withProviderRegistryLock(dir, () => scanProviderProcessSlotsUnlocked(dir, now, staleMs).live, lockTiming);
~
+}
~
~
+export function acquireProviderProcessSlot(
~
+  dir: string,
~
+  cap: number,
~
+  staleMs: number,
~
+  now: number,
~
+  meta: ProviderProcessSlotMeta,
~
+  lockTiming: ProviderRegistryLockTiming = {},
~
+  scanHooks: ProviderRegistryScanHooks = {},
~
+): AcquiredProviderProcessSlot | null {
~
+  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
~
+  const boundedCap = Number.isFinite(cap) && Number.isInteger(cap) && cap > 0
~
+    ? cap
~
+    : PROVIDER_PROCESS_MAX_CONCURRENT_DEFAULT;
~
+  return withProviderRegistryLock(dir, () => {
~
+    const scan = scanProviderProcessSlotsUnlocked(dir, now, staleMs, scanHooks);
~
+    if (scan.occupiedCount >= boundedCap) return null;
~
+    const token = randomUUID();
~
+    const record: ProviderProcessSlotFileMeta = { ...meta, token };
~
+    for (let index = 0; index < boundedCap; index += 1) {
~
+      const file = join(dir, `slot-${index}.json`);
~
+      if (writeProviderProcessSlotExclusive(file, record)) return { file, token };
~
+      const judged = readSlotOccupant(file);
~
+      if (!slotReclaimable(judged, file, now, staleMs)) continue;
~
+      if (judged.state !== 'missing') {
~
+        if (!sameSlotOccupant(readSlotOccupant(file), judged)) continue;
~
+        try { (scanHooks.unlinkForReclaim ?? unlinkSync)(file); } catch { /* absence is proven below */ }
~
+        // Do not move to another index after a failed reclaim: a live,
~
+        // corrupt, or inaccessible entry remains capacity until a fresh scan
~
+        // can prove it absent.
~
+        if (readSlotOccupant(file).state !== 'missing') continue;
~
+      }
~
+      if (writeProviderProcessSlotExclusive(file, record)) return { file, token };
~
+    }
~
+    return null;
~
+  }, lockTiming);
~
+}
~
~
+export function releaseProviderProcessSlot(
~
+  file: string | null,
~
+  token: string | null,
~
+  lockTiming: ProviderRegistryLockTiming = {},
~
+  mutationOps: ProviderRegistryMutationOps = DEFAULT_PROVIDER_REGISTRY_MUTATION_OPS,
~
+): void {
~
+  if (!file || !token) return;
~
+  const dir = dirname(file);
~
+  withProviderRegistryLock(dir, () => {
~
+    const occupant = readSlotOccupant(file);
~
+    if (occupant.state !== 'valid' || occupant.token !== token) return;
~
+    mutationOps.unlink(file);
~
+  }, lockTiming);
~
+}
~
~
+/**
~
+ * B-137a F-119: BEST-EFFORT release for `finally` blocks.
~
+ *
~
+ * Two correct-but-opposed requirements meet here:
~
+ *   1. A release failure must be OBSERVABLE, not a silent capacity leak --
~
+ *      releaseProviderProcessSlot therefore throws, and a registry smoke pins
~
+ *      that ("slot unlink mutation failure must be observable instead of
~
+ *      silently leaking capacity").
~
+ *   2. Every production release happens in a bare `finally` (host-run,
~
+ *      autopilot-executor, codex-review-leaf, provider-process-admission), and
~
+ *      a throw from `finally` REPLACES the in-flight exception -- hiding the
~
+ *      real provider failure -- or turns a successful run into a hard error.
~
+ *      host-run.ts's original releaseSlot wrapped its body in try/catch for
~
+ *      exactly this reason; a refactor dropped that.
~
+ *
~
+ * Swallowing inside the primitive would satisfy (2) by destroying (1). So the
~
+ * primitive keeps throwing and `finally` callers use this wrapper, which
~
+ * reports the failure through onFailure instead of hijacking control flow.
~
+ * Capacity is still reclaimable: pid-death detection and the orphan backstop
~
+ * recover a leaked slot, whereas a masked exception is unrecoverable.
~
+ */
~
+export function releaseProviderProcessSlotBestEffort(
~
+  file: string | null,
~
+  token: string | null,
~
+  onFailure: (error: unknown) => void = defaultReleaseFailureReporter,
~
+  lockTiming: ProviderRegistryLockTiming = {},
~
+  mutationOps: ProviderRegistryMutationOps = DEFAULT_PROVIDER_REGISTRY_MUTATION_OPS,
~
+): void {
~
+  try {
~
+    releaseProviderProcessSlot(file, token, lockTiming, mutationOps);
~
+  } catch (error) {
~
+    // Never rethrow: this runs in finally. Reporting must not fail either.
~
+    try {
~
+      onFailure(error);
~
+    } catch { /* a broken reporter must not mask the caller's exception */ }
~
+  }
~
+}
~
~
+function defaultReleaseFailureReporter(error: unknown): void {
~
+  const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
~
+  process.stderr.write(
~
+    `⚠ provider process slot release failed (capacity is reclaimed by pid-death / orphan backstop): ${detail}\n`,
~
+  );
~
+}
~
~
+export function transferProviderProcessSlotToProvider(
~
+  file: string | null,
~
+  token: string | null,
~
+  identity: {
~
+    pid: number;
~
+    pgid: number | null;
~
+    spawnedAt: string;
~
+    startFingerprint: string | null;
~
+    processGroupIsolated: boolean;
~
+  },
~
+  lockTiming: ProviderRegistryLockTiming = {},
~
+): boolean {
~
+  if (!file || !token) return false;
~
+  if (
~
+    !Number.isInteger(identity.pid) || identity.pid <= 0
~
+    || !identity.processGroupIsolated
~
+    || !Number.isInteger(identity.pgid) || (identity.pgid ?? 0) <= 0
~
+  ) return false;
~
+  const dir = dirname(file);
~
+  return withProviderRegistryLock(dir, () => {
~
+    const occupant = readSlotOccupant(file);
~
+    if (occupant.state !== 'valid' || occupant.token !== token) return false;
~
+    const next: ProviderProcessSlotFileMeta = {
~
+      ...(occupant.meta as unknown as ProviderProcessSlotFileMeta),
~
+      pid: identity.pid,
~
+      providerPid: identity.pid,
~
+      providerPgid: identity.pgid!,
~
+      providerSpawnedAt: identity.spawnedAt,
~
+      providerStartFingerprint: identity.startFingerprint ?? undefined,
~
+      providerProcessGroupIsolated: true,
~
+      token,
~
+    };
~
+    const temporary = `${file}.${token}.transfer`;
~
+    writeFileSync(temporary, JSON.stringify(next), { encoding: 'utf8', flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 });
~
+    try {
~
+      // Registry lock + exact token check makes this replacement ownership-safe.
~
+      renameSync(temporary, file);
~
+    } finally {
~
+      try { unlinkSync(temporary); } catch { /* rename already consumed it */ }
~
+    }
~
+    return true;
~
+  }, lockTiming);
~
+}

+  | 'admission_only'

+  | 'adapter_only'
~
+  | 'readiness_probe'
~
+  | 'legacy_unmanaged';

+/**
~
+ * Conservative source classifier used by the contract smoke. Any production
~
+ * file that imports a provider adapter, is itself an adapter, or combines a
~
+ * child-process API with provider vocabulary must have an explicit inventory
~
+ * row. False positives are classified, never silently excluded, so adding a
~
+ * new direct provider spawn in a new file makes the contract fail closed.
~
+ */
~
+export function isProviderExecutionSurfaceCandidate(relativePath: string, source: string): boolean {
~
+  if (!relativePath.endsWith('.ts')) return false;
~
+  if (/(?:^|\/)(?:tasks|tests|generated)(?:\/|$)/.test(relativePath)) return false;
~
+  if (relativePath === 'core/provider-process-registry.ts') return false;
~
+  if (/^providers\/(?:codex-cli|claude-cli|gemini-cli)\.ts$/.test(relativePath)) return true;
~
+  if (/providers\/(?:codex-cli|claude-cli|gemini-cli)\.js/.test(source)) return true;
~
+  if (/\brunHostRun\s*\(/.test(source)) return true;
~
+  // B-137a: strip documentation filename references before the provider-word
~
+  // scan. The words are matched case-insensitively, so a prose citation of
~
+  // "CLAUDE.md" (the project convention doc, referenced by many core modules)
~
+  // read as a provider reference: any file that both used child_process for git
~
+  // and cited that doc became an "unclassified provider execution surface".
~
+  // scope-contract.ts tripped exactly this way on a comment citing the handler
~
+  // convention -- a docs citation, not a provider workload. Several already
~
+  // inventoried files (audit-scan, audit-trigger, rollout-check,
~
+  // runtime-environment-checks) match for the same non-reason. Stripping only
~
+  // "<provider>.md" filenames keeps every real provider reference intact,
~
+  // including CLAUDE_CLI, claudeCli, 'claude' and providers/claude-cli.js.
~
+  const withoutDocReferences = source.replace(/\b(?:codex|claude|agy|gemini|antigravity)\.md\b/gi, '');
~
+  // Demand a real child-process launch whose *argument* carries provider
~
+  // identity. A module can legitimately run Git (or its own lifecycle hooks)
~
+  // while describing Codex or Claude elsewhere in comments and diagnostics;
~
+  // treating that co-occurrence as a provider launch made the inventory claim
~
+  // false positives. Preserve identifier forms such as `claudeCli`, command
~
+  // variables such as `const command = 'codex'; spawn(command)`, and the
~
+  // common mapping/resolver forms by tracing the first argument one bounded
~
+  // lexical hop before classifying an otherwise unresolved launch conservatively.
~
+  const importsChildProcess = /(?:\bfrom\s*|\brequire\s*\(\s*|\bimport\s*)(['"])(?:node:)?child_process\1/.test(source);
~
+  if (!importsChildProcess) return false;
~
+  const launchApi = '(?:spawn|spawnSync|execFile|execFileSync|exec)';
~
+  const aliasNames = new Set<string>();
~
+  const aliasPatterns = [
~
+    new RegExp(`\\b${launchApi}\\s+as\\s+([A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*)`, 'g'),
~
+    new RegExp(`\\b${launchApi}\\s*:\\s*([A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*)`, 'g'),
~
+    new RegExp(`\\b(?:const|let|var)\\s+([A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*)\\s*=\\s*[A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*\\s*\\.\\s*${launchApi}\\b`, 'g'),
~
+  ];
~
+  for (const pattern of aliasPatterns) {
~
+    for (const match of withoutDocReferences.matchAll(pattern)) aliasNames.add(match[1]!);
~
+  }
~
+  // Comments are not launch sites. Strip them only after collecting import and
~
+  // alias bindings, because an import / alias itself is source syntax rather
~
+  // than a comment-derived provider word.
~
+  const launchSource = withoutDocReferences.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|\/\/[^\r\n]*/g, '');
~
+  const aliasApi = [...aliasNames].map(name => name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')).join('|');
~
+  const launchCallee = aliasApi.length > 0
~
+    ? `(?:${launchApi}|[A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*\\s*\\.\\s*${launchApi}|${aliasApi})`
~
+    : `(?:${launchApi}|[A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*\\s*\\.\\s*${launchApi})`;
~
+  const providerToken = /(?:codex|claude|agy|gemini|antigravity)/i;
~
+  const launchCall = new RegExp(`\\b${launchCallee}\\s*\\(\\s*([^,\\r\\n)]*)`, 'g');
~
+  const sourceNamesProvider = (name: string): boolean => {
~
+    const escapedName = name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
~
+    // Bounded object-map lookup: `const PROVIDER_COMMAND = { codex: ... }`
~
+    // plus `const command = PROVIDER_COMMAND[host]` must not hide a spawn.
~
+    const objectMap = new RegExp(`\\b(?:const|let|var)\\s+${escapedName}\\s*=\\s*\\{[\\s\\S]{0,8192}?(?:codex|claude|agy|gemini|antigravity)`, 'i');
~
+    if (objectMap.test(launchSource)) return true;
~
+    // Bounded resolver lookup: `command = resolveProviderCommand(host)` and
~
+    // a local resolver body with provider selection are likewise a provider
~
+    // command even when no literal reaches spawn's first argument.
~
+    const resolver = new RegExp(`\\b(?:function\\s+${escapedName}\\s*\\([^)]*\\)\\s*\\{|(?:const|let|var)\\s+${escapedName}\\s*=\\s*(?:async\\s*)?\\([^)]*\\)\\s*=>\\s*\\{?)[\\s\\S]{0,8192}?(?:codex|claude|agy|gemini|antigravity)`, 'i');
~
+    return resolver.test(launchSource);
~
+  };
~
+  for (const match of launchSource.matchAll(launchCall)) {
~
+    const firstArgument = match[1]!.trim();
~
+    if (providerToken.test(firstArgument)) return true;
~
+    // Handle direct forms too: `spawn(PROVIDER_COMMANDS[host], ...)` and
~
+    // `spawn(resolveProviderCommand(host), ...)` do not allocate a neutral
~
+    // local identifier for the one-hop initializer logic below.
~
+    const directMapName = firstArgument.match(/^([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*(?:\[|\.)/)?.[1];
~
+    if (directMapName && sourceNamesProvider(directMapName)) return true;
~
+    const directResolverName = firstArgument.match(/^([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/)?.[1];
~
+    if (directResolverName && sourceNamesProvider(directResolverName)) return true;
~
+    const identifier = firstArgument.match(/^([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)$/)?.[1];
~
+    if (!identifier) continue;
~
+    const escapedIdentifier = identifier.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
~
+    const initializer = new RegExp(`\\b(?:const|let|var)\\s+${escapedIdentifier}\\s*=\\s*([^;\\r\\n]+)`, 'i').exec(launchSource)?.[1];
~
+    if (!initializer) continue;
~
+    if (providerToken.test(initializer)) return true;
~
+    const mapName = initializer.match(/^([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*(?:\[|\.)/)?.[1];
~
+    if (mapName && sourceNamesProvider(mapName)) return true;
~
+    const resolverName = initializer.match(/^([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/)?.[1];
~
+    if (resolverName && sourceNamesProvider(resolverName)) return true;
~
+  }
~
+  return false;
~
+}

+function assertOnlyKeys(command: string, value: Record<string, unknown>, allowed: readonly string[]): void {
~
+  const unexpected = Object.keys(value).filter(key => !allowed.includes(key));
~
+  if (unexpected.length > 0) {

+    throw new Error(`${command}: unexpected fields ${unexpected.sort().join(', ')}; verdict overrides are not accepted`);

+/**
~
+ * The importer owns only review-passes/findings plus its optional process
~
+ * event. The importer stages only its exact artifacts, but an already-staged
~
+ * index can still be committed by an implementation regression. Refuse that
~
+ * state before intake; ordinary untracked/unstaged story state remains safe
~
+ * because the exact-path auto-commit allowlist cannot sweep it into the commit.
~
+ */
~
+function assertManagedReviewImportStagingClean(ctx: HandlerContext, storyId: string, gitCwd: string): void {

~
+  const storyDir = ctx.store.storyDirPath(storyId);
~
+  const storyPath = relative(gitCwd, storyDir);
~
+  if (!storyPath || storyPath === '.' || storyPath === '..' || storyPath.startsWith('../')) {
~
+    throw new Error('managed_review_evidence_import: story metadata directory is outside the canonical git workspace');
~
+  }
~
+  const staged = execFileSync('git', ['diff', '--cached', '--name-only', '--', storyPath], {
~
+    cwd: gitCwd,
~
+    encoding: 'utf8',
~
+    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
~
+  }).trim();
~
+  if (staged) {
~
+    throw new Error('managed_review_evidence_import: story metadata has staged changes; refuse an importer transaction that could commit adjacent artifacts');
~
+  }
~
+}

~
+    managed_review_proposal_set(args: {

Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.

The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
that never used the managed boundary.

## Why this exists

A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.

Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
phase.

## `host_run`

```
lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
  [--json]
```

`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:

```bash
lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
```

`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
cleanup made replacement safe.

An ordinary host run executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
never diverge from where the ledger says it ran. A formal `--managedReview` is
different: the runtime-artifact registry resolves the canonical **primary
worktree** as the durable runtime/audit root for the sealed run, output journal,
terminal receipt, receipt archive, and imported evidence. A linked Story
worktree may submit the run, but is not the durable runtime location and can be
removed at DONE. The provider executes only in a fresh detached scratch
worktree at the submitted HEAD. The scratch is read-only for Codex and is
retained until terminal cleanup is proven replacement-safe; it is never a
substitute for the audit root.

Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
caller as it arrives, up to the per-run 8 MiB retention ceiling. The foreground
projection is explicitly bounded: once the ceiling is reached, `--json` reports
`truncated=true` on the `lattice.host_run.v1` result and text mode writes
`truncated=true` to stderr; neither promises the omitted tail.
`host_run_status --json` exposes the same flag as `output.truncated`. Worker
heartbeat and `lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
is written to stderr, for example:

```
usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
```

Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
perfectly good final usage event).

### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)

| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |

In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the JSON result reports
`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail; the JSON `stdout` field
carries only the bounded usage-parse tail, not an unbounded or complete
transcript.

If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
fires while a listener is attached. If the drain cap wins, one shared guard stays
per physical stream until each pending write settles; its release is deferred
through the next event-loop turn because Node `Writable` can invoke the write
callback before emitting the same failed write's `EPIPE` event. This contains the real
callback-then-error ordering without retaining one listener per foreground run.

Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.

### Reviewer launch

Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.

An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
registered broker set.

`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers` is an object containing a `brokers` array. Each
registration has all four required fields: `brokerId` (the unique trusted broker
name), `adapterId` (the adapter identity the attestation claims), `host` (exactly
`"codex"` or `"claude"`), and `publicKey` (the broker's Ed25519 public key).

  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimable at any age only
  after its isolated provider PGID is also confirmed absent; a dead supervisor
  whose provider group remains live still consumes capacity and is retained.
  A slot whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between
  creating the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime
  exceeds the `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default
  **6h**); a fresh non-reclaimable corrupt slot also consumes capacity (even at
  a high index after a cap is lowered), although it has no safe descriptor to
  render in the live-run list; a slot with a **live** recorded pid is **never
  reclaimed by age** — a long host run keeps its admission and waiters refuse
  at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
  counts every non-reclaimable high-index slot and refuses new starts until the
  total occupied count drops below the new cap.

Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the managed
host that was asked to run (`openai` for codex or `anthropic` for claude), never
a hard-coded default.

modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
after the run.

/**
 * Evaluate canonical read-only report projections before a managed provider is
 * launched. This stays in the controller's signed primary worktree; the
 * returned snapshot is deliberately a bounded, path-free provider projection.
 */
export function collectManagedReviewCanonicalReportStatuses(
  ctx: HandlerContext,
  storyId: string,
): ManagedReviewCanonicalReportStatus[] {
  return [
    managedReviewReportStatus('acceptance_topology_check', () => evaluateAcceptanceTopologyForContext(ctx, storyId)),
    managedReviewReportStatus('pre_review_check_read', () => evaluatePreReviewCheckForContext(ctx, storyId)),
    managedReviewReportStatus('acceptance_rollout_report_read', () => evaluateAcceptanceRolloutForContext(ctx, storyId)),
    managedReviewReportStatus('acceptance_rollout_check', () => evaluateAcceptanceRolloutForContext(ctx, storyId)),
  ];
}

  storyId: string | null,
  explicitPhase: string | undefined,
  resolveStory: HostRunStoryResolver | undefined,
): string {
  if (storyId === null) return explicitPhase && explicitPhase.length > 0 ? explicitPhase : 'adhoc';
  if (explicitPhase && explicitPhase.length > 0) return explicitPhase;
  if (!resolveStory) {
    throw new Error(
      `host_run: cannot resolve a phase for story "${storyId}" without --phase and without a configured story resolver `
      + '(internal: the handler must inject resolveStory); pass --phase or run adhoc',
    );
  }
  const meta = resolveStory(storyId);

function assertReviewRunIdBinding(
  storyId: string | null,
  reviewRunId: string | null | undefined,
): void {
  if (!reviewRunId) return;
  if (storyId && !reviewRunId.startsWith(`${storyId}:`)) {
    throw new Error(
      `host_run: reviewRunId "${reviewRunId}" does not belong to story "${storyId}" `
      + '(a reviewRunId must be "<storyId>:..."); refuse pre-spawn to avoid a cross-story ledger mis-join',
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Scan codex `exec --json` stdout for the LAST `{"type":"turn.completed",
 * "usage":{...}}` event and return its raw usage object (own-property guarded),
 * or null when no turn.completed usage event is present. Line-streamed with a
 * BOUNDED parse buffer: only the current line and the last usage object are held,
 * so a flooding host cannot accumulate per-line state.
